title: indie-ads catalogue
description: The games that can be advertised and their creatives. Relative paths are read against the catalogue's own URL. core/catalogue.js enforces this at run time, dropping a bad entry rather than failing.

signedBy.description: The public key of whoever signs this catalogue as it is served (ECDSA P-256, base64url), written by the server. A game believes it only from the copy it shipped with.

more.description: The network's page of its games: https, ending in a / (a game's id follows it): what the link to more games behind an ad's ⓘ opens, with the id of the game showing the ad. Left out: no such link.

pt.description: Our App Store provider token, used in campaign links for apps marked own.

exchange.description: What share of a host game's ad slots the network asks for, when the host has a paid network to show instead (core/exchange.js). Left out: none.

share.description: Asked of a host whose studio owes no one. 0–1.

max.description: Asked of a host whose studio owes `full` showings or more. 0–1.

full.description: The debt, in showings, at which `max` is reached.

perDay.description: The most house ads one player is shown in 24 hours in one game, counted on the device. Left out: no limit.

fatigue.description: A game whose ads a player has been shown `after` times with no store tap rests (isn't shown to them) for `rest` days, `grow` times longer each time again, at most 180 days. A store tap starts it over. Counted on the device. Left out: after 6, rest 14, grow 2.

after.description: Showings with no store tap. 0: never rests.

hosts.description: share / max / full / perDay / fatigue for one host, by its id; and `placements`, a share / max per placement of it.

minSecs.description: The least time this host's placements hold a player to an ad, in seconds, for each kind of placement, in place of what the game's code says; a placement's own (`placements.<id>.minSecs`) comes before it. Read from 0.6.3.

placements.description: By the placement's id, as the host names it. A placement given a share and no max stays at that share, whatever is owed. `minSecs` is its own, with or without a share.

minSecs.description: The least time this placement holds a player to an ad, in seconds, in place of what the game's code says. Read from 0.6.3.

apps.description: One record per game, keyed by its id. A host game's id here is what it passes as `host`.

studio.description: The id of the studio whose game it is: what the exchange counts by, and a game is weighted double in the games of its own studio. Never shown.

studioName.description: What that studio is called, shown small on the end card. Left out: nothing is shown.

own.description: The network's own game: its App Store links carry the catalogue's provider token (pt). A game released before 0.3.2 also weights it double and shows it to players under 13.

under13.description: May be shown to a player known to be under 13. Left out, it is as own says.

line.description: One line about the game, for the end card when a creative has none. One string for everyone, or one per language: { "en": "…", "fr": "…", "es-419": "…" }.

art.description: Key art behind the end card.

rating.description: The age its ads suit: "4+", "9+", "13+"… A game rated below it shows none of them. It is what the creatives show, which is often less than the game's own store rating; where they differ among themselves, the lowest of theirs.

status.description: "preorder": the button says Pre-order / Pre-register until `release`.

scheme.description: A URL scheme the game registers. Read only by releases before 0.3.0, which asked iOS whether the game was installed; no longer used.

pt.description: This app's own provider token, if not ours.

web.description: The game's own page, where the button goes when the game isn't on the player's store, or on any yet (a prototype, a playtest sign-up). Opened in the browser.

label.description: What the button says, in the player's language. Default learnMore.

tracking.description: The partner's attribution click link, used instead of a store link. Macros: {host} {campaign} {creative} {placement}. One for both stores, or one each.

secs.description: A video's length; how long a playable runs before the reward.

src.description: video: MP4, H.264 + AAC. playable: one self-contained HTML file, MRAID 2/3.

poster.description: video: a still, shown before it plays and blurred behind it.

aspect.description: The shape of screen it is made for: a video's own shape, or the way up a playable is meant to be held. Left out, it suits any host.

line.description: One line for the end card. One string, or one per language, as an app's.

langs.description: Only for players in these languages ("en", "es"): for a creative with words in it. Left out: for all.

finishEarly.description: playable: the reward lands when it calls mraid.close(), if that's before `secs`.

ownCard.description: It ends on an end card of its own, so the player's isn't shown. video: it rests on its last frame, with the store button alone over it (the player's words, or `storeButton`'s picture), and the video itself opens nothing unless `tap.whole` says from when. playable: its own card and store button are in its page (mraid.open()); when `secs` are up the reward is in and it plays on until closed, and `keepPlaying` has nothing to do. Read from 0.6.2: a release before plays either as any other creative, the player's card at its end.

ownEndCard.description: How `ownCard` was said of a video before 0.6.2, with one difference: there's no store button, and a tap anywhere on the video, at any time, opens the store. Players tap through without meaning to: say `ownCard`. Still read, for a catalogue that says it.

keepPlaying.description: playable: when `secs` are up it's paused under the end card (told it isn't viewable, volume 0), which offers Keep playing, for up to 2 minutes more. Only for a page that pauses when told.

rating.description: The age this creative suits, where it differs from its app's. A game shows it only if this and its app's rating are both no higher than the game's own, so an app with creatives rated apart carries the lowest of them.

to.description: The first day it no longer shows.

hosts.description: Only in these host games. Left out: in all.

os.description: Only on this platform. Left out: on both. Read from 0.6.18: a release before shows it on both, so the network's server gives those releases none of these.

campaign.description: The campaign name in store links. Left out: the creative's id.

endCardMode.description: Use matching-orientation endcard art. No image for this orientation: the default card. Video images fit the video stage and keep its backdrop. Display controls use the current UI with or without this field.

endCardSecs.description: Minimum visible seconds on the ending before X can close, independent of reward timing. Pauses when hidden or in a store/info panel. Defaults to 3; zero allows immediate close once eligible.

endCardCta.description: Endcard CTA independent of static frame, loop or custom art. Large centres app details; compact uses the bottom app link. Custom is retained for earlier catalogue records.

during.description: Show the bottom app link while the video plays, independently of the ending style.

darken.description: Large style: darken behind the app details.

fade.description: Fixed 0.5-second CTA fade-in when enabled. Zero/false disables it; older positive durations are normalised to 0.5. An already-visible app link does not restart fading.

anchor.description: The edge or corner it's set against.

x.description: How far in from the anchor's side; from a centre, to the right.

y.description: How far in from the anchor's top or bottom; from the middle, down.

endCard.description: Art for the end card, by the screen's shape: either stands in for the other. Left out: the player's own card (icon, name, line). Read from 0.5.0; a release before it shows its own card.

storeButton.description: The store button on the end card. Left out: the player's own, in the player's language, where it has always been. Read from 0.5.0.

ios.description: A picture of the button for the App Store (PNG). Left out: the player's own button, in words.

pulse.description: It swells and settles, to be seen: true (once a second, to 1.05 of its size), or how.

loop.description: video: at its end it plays on from `from` seconds, silent, behind the store button, where the end card would stand. Read from 0.5.0.

tap.description: video: when a tap opens the store. Each is seconds in, or "end": with the end card. Read from 0.5.0.

button.description: When the store button is there. Left out: from the start.

whole.description: From when a tap anywhere on the video opens the store. Left out: never.

overrun.description: video: it may be shown in a placement shorter than it (`maxSecs` under its `secs`). The reward comes at the placement's time, and the video plays on: the player may watch to its end or leave by the end card. Read from 0.5.0; a release before it shows the video only where it fits.

minSecs.description: playable: the earliest second it may be left at, no later than `secs`, which is how long it plays. What `skipFrom` is to a video, under a name of its own because a release from 0.6.3 to 0.6.7 takes `skipFrom` for a video's alone. Rewarded: the reward comes then, or at the placement's own least time if that is later, and the playable plays on to its time; its ✓ before then is to its end card. Interstitial: it isn't shown in a placement whose least time is shorter than this. It may also be shown in a placement shorter than it (`maxSecs`), if it may be left by then. Left out: its reward comes at its time, and an interstitial is the placement's to time. Read from 0.6.8; a release before plays it as one without.

skipFrom.description: video: the earliest second it may be left at; no later than `secs`. Rewarded: the reward comes then, or at the placement's own least time (`minSecs`) if that is later, and the player may leave for the end card. Interstitial: it isn't shown in a placement whose least time is shorter than this. It may also be shown in a placement shorter than it (`maxSecs`), if it may be left by then. Left out: a rewarded one is watched to its end unless the placement says a time, and an interstitial is the placement's to time. Read from 0.6.3; a release before plays it as one without.

aspectOnly.description: With `aspect`: it is shown only where the screen is that shape. Left out: a screen of the other shape may be shown it too (a video letterboxed), at half its weight. Read from 0.6.8; a release before shows it either way.

fade.description: video: the seconds at its end over which the end card comes up and the sound goes down. Left out: none, a cut. Read from 0.5.0.

backdrop.description: video: what's behind it where it doesn't fill the screen. "video": its own picture, blurred, as it plays. Left out: its poster, blurred. Read from 0.5.0.

place.description: Where the store button is, for a screen of this shape. Lengths are in units of 1/720 of the screen's shorter side, so it's the same on a phone and a tablet.

anchor.description: The edge or corner it's set against.

x.description: How far in from the anchor's side; from a centre, to the right.

y.description: How far in from the anchor's top or bottom; from the middle, down.
